deep.reconstruction:
This page is a heavily corrected pencil draft of the analysis-situs preliminaries to Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). Its content corresponds to the published sections 'Lehrsätze aus der analysis situs für die Theorie der Integrale von zweigliedrigen vollständigen Differentialen'. The draft is written on the back of a printed ledger form with columns Auslage/Porto/Franko. The page does three things.

(1) Definition and main lemma (top lines). A surface T is called n-fold connected ('n fach zusammenhängend') in Riemann's sense. A cross-cut (Querschnitt) is a cut running through the interior from one boundary point to another. The lemma: an n-fold connected surface is turned into an (n-1)-fold connected one by every cross-cut that does not separate it into disjoint pieces.
In modern terms, Riemann's order of connectivity is n = 1 + rank H_1(T) = 2 - chi(T) for a compact surface with nonempty boundary. Cutting along a properly embedded arc raises chi by 1. So a non-separating cut lowers n by exactly 1. (The Euler-characteristic formulation is mine, not Riemann's.)

(2) Sketch of proof (the heavily struck middle block, only partly legible). The argument works with closed curves ('in sich zurücklaufende Linie') and with the parts of the boundary into which the cut divides things ('Begrenzungstheile'). It considers a closed curve 'a' and a curve 'b', the course of a running through that of b. The idea is to compare systems of closed curves that together form the complete boundary of a part of T, before and after the cut.
The intended point appears to be this. A closed curve meeting the cross-cut once, together with the cut, lets every bounding system in the cut surface be related to one in the uncut surface and conversely. So the number of independent non-bounding closed curves drops by exactly one. This is the argument of the published §1, but here it is too fragmentary to reconstruct line by line.

(3) Corollaries.
- An (n+1)-fold connected surface becomes n-fold connected by every non-separating cross-cut.
- A surface not cut into pieces by a cross-cut can be cut further.
- Iterating the process, an (n+1)-fold connected surface becomes simply connected after n cross-cuts. Equivalently, an n-fold connected surface becomes simply connected after n-1 cuts.
- A following struck passage seems to add that the same holds if the cutting is done in a different order or with different cuts: the number of cuts is an invariant. This is the published statement that connectivity is independent of the choice of cuts.

(4) Application (bottom). The dissection into simply connected pieces is applied to integrals of the form ∫(X dx + Y dy). Let T be a surface covering the (x,y)-plane, on which X and Y are continuous functions of position satisfying ∂X/∂y - ∂Y/∂x = 0. If T is n-fold connected, it is cut by n-1 cross-cuts into a simply connected surface T'.
The sentence breaks off at 'Die Integration ...'. The intended continuation, known from the published paper, is as follows. On T' the integral ∫(X dx + Y dy) from a fixed point is a single-valued function of the endpoint. Across each cut it jumps by a constant, the period, which is the same along the whole cut. There are thus n-1 periods. The next page (159) turns to the Dirichlet principle for determining a function of x+iy in T.
errors: No mathematical errors are detectable in the legible parts. The index conventions ('n fach' becoming 'n-1 fach' with one cut; 'n+1 fach' needing n cuts; 'n fach' needing n-1 cuts) are mutually consistent.

The proof sketch in the middle is left incomplete and heavily struck. As written it does not constitute a full proof that a non-separating cut lowers connectivity by exactly one, nor of the invariance of the number of cuts. These are drafts of the arguments printed in 1857, whose rigor was later questioned (e.g. by Tonelli and Weyl, who refined the notion of connectivity).

results.what: A non-separating cross-cut lowers the order of connectivity of a surface by one
results.modern_name: Cutting along a non-separating properly embedded arc increases Euler characteristic by 1 (connectivity = first Betti number + 1)

results.what: An (n+1)-fold connected surface becomes simply connected after n cross-cuts, independent of the choice of cuts
results.modern_name: Riemann's order of connectivity / canonical dissection; topological invariance of the first Betti number

results.what: Application to the closed differential X dx + Y dy with ∂X/∂y = ∂Y/∂x on an n-fold connected surface: single-valued integral on the cut surface, constant jumps (periods) across the cuts
results.modern_name: Periods of closed 1-forms; de Rham-type duality between H^1 and cycles
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, 1857 (with antecedents in Gauss/Cauchy for plane domains)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of the well-known analysis-situs section of Riemann's 1857 Abelian functions paper (connectivity, cross-cuts, application to exact differentials). The content is published and credited to him. The draft only documents its genesis.

checkable.asserts: Example (mine): this X dx + Y dy satisfies the integrability condition ∂X/∂y - ∂Y/∂x = 0 away from the origin. The result is 0.
The same form integrated around the unit circle gives 2*pi, not 0. So on the 2-fold connected annulus one cross-cut is needed to make the integral single-valued, and the period is 2*pi.
With connectivity n = 2 - chi, a cut along an arc (chi -> chi+1) lowers n by exactly 1, matching 'n fach -> n-1 fach'.
For a genus-p surface with b>=1 boundary circles, Riemann's connectivity 2 - chi equals 2p+b. The expression is 0.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'durch welchen sie {+nicht+} in getrennte Stücke zerschnitten' is the intended reading. The insertion 'nicht' is essential: the cut must not separate the surface.
The printed header ('Auslage', 'Porto', 'Franko', columns ₰/M) belongs to a ledger form used as scrap paper and is not part of the text.

Bottom: the condition reads ∂X/∂y - ∂Y/∂x = 0, with symbols written as dX/dy, dY/dx in the margin. The surface T has X, Y as 'stetige' functions of position, and the cut count is 'n-1' for an n-fold connected surface.
The struck marginal formula at the bottom left is '∫(X dx + Y dy)', the heading of the application paragraph.
